page: Vultr voc-g-2c-8gb-50s-amd is an instance within the Optimized Cloud Compute family, featuring an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC processor. The server is configured with 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz under a shared CPU allocation model. It includes 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and is equipped with 50 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The network configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates a divergence between raw single-core compute and overall system throughput. The server achieves top-tier performance in stress-ng single-core CPU testing, ranking in the top 10%, while its multi-core CPU performance falls into the average range. Conversely, memory and database performance show notable limitations. Passmark CPU scores, encryption tests, and physics tests are positioned in the bottom 25%. Database operations and static web serving throughput are particularly constrained, registering in the bottom 10% of benchmarks. Redis SET operations and prompt processing for small language models also rank in the bottom 25%, though text generation for a small 135M model reaches average speeds.

Given its shared CPU allocation and modest memory bandwidth, this instance offers a cost-effective entry point for workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated CPU performance. The 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and local NVMe storage make it suitable for general-purpose utility tasks, lightweight application hosting, development environments, and basic text processing. However, the poor database and web serving throughput benchmarks suggest it is less suitable for high-traffic production databases or high-concurrency web servers.
